title: The Verb Spine
subtitle: קאל · כאן · the prefix conjugation
intro: Two verbs hold the Tafsir together: קאל "he said" (every speech is introduced by it) and כאן "he was" (the workhorse of "there was / it became"). Learn how they flex and the narrative stops looking opaque. Arabic marks the subject two ways — by an ending on the past tense, and by a prefix on the present.

sections.heading: Past tense: the ending carries the subject
sections.body: The bare 3rd-person-masculine form is the dictionary form. Add an ending for she / they.

examples.note: The default form — what you'll meet most.

sections.heading: Present / future: the prefix carries the subject
sections.body: The imperfect adds a prefix: י־ (he), ת־ (she / you m.), נ־ (we), א־ (I). Same letters as the Hebrew prefix conjugation.

sections.heading: כאן — "was" and "became"
sections.body: כאן sets the scene: "there was," "it was," "it became." Its present יכון means "is / will be." You'll meet it in the second verse of the Tafsir.

quiz.explanation: קאל = qāla, "he said" — the verb that introduces nearly every speech.

quiz.q: The prefix in יקול tells you the subject is…

quiz.explanation: כאן = kāna, "was / became" — the scene-setting verb.

quiz.q: Which is the present/future of כאן?
